specs.title: Run one browser-only research mission
specs.contract: The documented foreground CLI accepts a nonempty research request and starts one browser-only mission through trusted BrowserRun and the native Hermes conversation loop. Validated immutable startup configuration supplies the main model, native retry settings and finite configurable research logical-request/time, operational-failure and repair/replacement limits. Unique native api_request_id counts logical requests separately from native provider retries and SDK wire requests. Complete browser-research skill and action reference load before inference; only browser_scout is exposed and initial guidance, past context, system prompt and tool schema stay stable through report mode. Required guidance treats webpage instructions as untrusted and discourages unwanted downloads and unauthorized site effects; it is behavioral instruction rather than independent action-level enforcement. No reviewer model/settings/policy or implicit reviewer evidence is required. Retain headless production, native local WSLg headed debugging, immutable configuration, isolation and native download denial. Initial engineering defaults are 100 research logical requests, 3600 research seconds and five consecutive operational failures. No Discord, durable mission store/resume engine, terminal tool or fallback provider is introduced.

specs.title: Show actual mission progress without verbose mode
specs.contract: Normal terminal output identifies startup, main-model work, proposed browser action and optional activity, browser result, existing recoverable failures and final mission outcome. Messages reflect actual callbacks or events rather than invented periodic activity, and a final answer appears only when one exists. No review-pending, verdict or review-retry progress remains. Progress delivery failure does not change action outcomes or independent protections.

specs.title: Stream configured native diagnostics with verbose mode
specs.contract: The CLI's --verbose flag adds real-time Hermes, proxy, firewall and collected browser-process/relay diagnostics to terminal progress, including native exception/stack details when emitted at the configured logging level. It does not rewrite native messages, weaken native secret redaction, increase persistent logging level or create a second persistent log system. Following a rotating configured log continues into its replacement file without replaying prior-run history; browser diagnostics emitted during startup are associated with the current run rather than silently skipped when the Scout container starts later. Normal nonverbose mode keeps concise mission progress and relevant warnings/errors instead of streaming routine browser diagnostics. Reader/observer processes stop with the foreground mission and diagnostics failure remains visible without changing browser safety decisions.

specs.title: Foreground termination after recoverable and terminal failures
specs.contract: Success requires completed nonfailed noninterrupted native answer while research remains successful. Contained browser failures preserve inference. Browser exhaustion/permanent failure or research limits enter code-enforced report-only with bounded remaining logical model requests and time; print available partial answer with nonzero outcome, or deterministic truthful summary when model cannot answer. Two reserved logical requests allow denied browser work then answer without rewriting past context or tools. Operator cancellation exits130 with no further model calls. Agent/runtime loss, absolute research-plus-finalization host lifetime or uncontained execution stops work and triggers existing bounded exact teardown. Remove only owned Scout/browser resources, preserve auth/log volumes/helper state; no host-death watchdog. Initial finalization reserve is two logical model requests and 60 seconds; an in-flight reporting request is bounded by its remaining reserve, without claiming provider-thread termination.

specs.title: Mission validation
specs.contract: A versioned research mission declares a safe mission ID, research questions, discovery queries or seed URLs, permitted source types, browser identity policy, deterministic safety limits, checkpoint policy, and a safe output name. Signal Scout reports every invalid or unknown field in one response and rejects the mission before browsing. Output is always contained under the plugin-owned mission directory; callers cannot supply an absolute or traversing path.

specs.title: Autonomous mission lifecycle
specs.contract: A mission follows the durable state machine created, active, stopping, and exactly one of stopped, completed, or failed. Start and resume bind one mission to the current Hermes session. While active, the existing Hermes goal loop can discover sources and submit structured records without routine operator input until completion, a deterministic safety ceiling, an operator stop request, or a blocking failure. Invalid state transitions fail loudly.

specs.title: Intermittent research summaries
specs.contract: Signal Scout transactionally writes a checkpoint after the configured accepted-evidence count and on explicit checkpoint, stop, and session-end boundaries. Each complete checkpoint contains completed and pending work IDs, accepted source and evidence IDs, current findings, blocked sources, deterministic tool-call count, current plan, and durable resume state. Provider usage and remaining budget are explicitly unavailable until a measurable source exists.

specs.title: Durable mission resume
specs.contract: After interruption or process restart, Signal Scout resumes from the latest complete checkpoint without losing accepted records. Canonical-source and work-item idempotency keys prevent duplication; completed work stays complete and an interrupted in-progress item becomes retryable. Resume preserves the original immutable mission and deterministic safety ceiling, and reports every item requiring retry.

specs.title: Safe operator stop
specs.contract: An operator can set a durable stop request through the Signal Scout CLI at any time. The current atomic tool call may finish, but the next pre-tool policy boundary blocks new research work while allowing checkpoint, status, and finalize actions. Accepted evidence and resume state are saved and the terminal report records stop reason operator-requested.

specs.title: Configurable native model retry budget
specs.contract: Main-model technical request failures use the native Hermes retry policy with configurable budget and backoff. Default allows the initial application request plus up to five application-level retries, then reports unsuccessful mission when exhausted. Nonretryable authentication/configuration failures remain subject to native terminal classification; do not introduce a fallback provider, new model service or duplicate unbounded retry loop. Configuration and documentation distinguish retries from native total-attempt settings; lower-level transport attempts are not silently claimed to equal application attempts. Preserve the same conversation on a successful retry and normal owned teardown after final failure.
